parallel.requirements: Recognized exact C++ output, stoi prefix parsing, i32 wrapping, std-only implementation, Cargo layout, root test11.rs, and black-box behavior constraints.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership, created task tracker entries for implementation and verification, and launched background design and verifier workflows.
parallel.implementation: Implemented persistent vector trie modules, C++ compatibility shims, Cargo.toml, and root test11.rs, then fixed debug and boundary issues found locally.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the parent-authored modules into one Cargo project and produced artifact files accepted by official artifact validation.
parallel.verification: Ran local compile checks, cargo tests, 4101-case differential sweep, runtime edge checks, and a background adversarial verifier that did not complete.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official functional defect remained, but verifier workflow result was null, design workflow also killed, parent timed out, and final.txt was empty.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same exact Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo, CLI, wrapping arithmetic, and byte-identical output requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor owned probing, implementation, testing, dependency audit, and final response without delegation or workflow children.
serial.implementation: Built persistent vector and C++ semantics modules, root test11.rs, Cargo.toml, and an executable matching reference behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all modules in the submitted project, listed output files, and delivered a final explanation of artifact placement.
serial.verification: Completed cargo build/test, exhaustive small/boundary/parser checks, 400 randomized byte-exact differential checks, dependency audit, and performance smoke test.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved workflow, no timeout, and no official functional defect; serial closed normally and passed 38/38.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo project, black-box behavior, exact output, and root test11.rs requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same C++ semantics and deliverable requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage outcome difference; both passed, though parallel also delegated design and verifier subtasks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split implementation, verification, and design/audit work across task trackers and background workflows while the parent kept implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification in one actor without child delegation or workflow ownership transfer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced delegated verifier ownership that later needed takeover; serial had a simpler single-owner path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verifier and design workflow briefs included rich task context, expected files, requirements, and reference-binary access.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all task context locally while implementing modules and C++ shims.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing task brief or interface contract caused incompatible work; the material difference was lifecycle takeover after a workflow abort.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a modular Rust project with persistent vector trie modules, C++ stoi/cint/cli shims, root test11.rs, and Cargo.toml.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a similar modular project with persistent vector modules, C++ parsing/terminate shims, Cargo.toml, and root test11.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations differ in module naming and details, but both satisfied the evaluator; no ordinary implementation defect explains an outcome gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched a background verifier workflow, continued local checks, then the verifier workflow was killed with result null and no parent takeover before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed its own build/test/differential results and proceeded directly to a final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete lifecycle difference is the unfinished parallel verifier workflow versus serial inline closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the deliverable files itself; child workflows mostly read/audited or designed and did not prove a file collision or overwrite in the submitted artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all deliverable files in one workspace and performed final file/dependency inspection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state merge conflict explains the result; both artifacts were copied and evaluated successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran extensive local differential sweeps and runtime edge checks, but the delegated adversarial verifier did not return an aggregate result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Cargo build/test, exhaustive and randomized differential checks, final dependency audit, and summarized those checks before closing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both were accepted officially, but serial completed and reported its verification loop while parallel left the delegated verifier unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted the full run window and exited with returncode 143 after 2400.264 seconds with an empty final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 910.986 seconds with returncode 0 and retained more than 1400 seconds of cell budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel workflow budget/closure problem did not change the official pass result, but it left process closure and delegated verification incomplete.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both modes passing 38/38, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is process and closure: parallel produced a passing artifact while leaving an aborted verifier workflow untaken-over and no final response; serial produced a passing artifact and completed inline verification and final reporting.

ordinary_implementation_differences: Different internal module naming and verification breadth did not produce an official outcome difference.

The parent owned the end-to-end implementation, local verification, and artifact delivery pipeline even though a later verifier workflow was not taken over.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent probed behavior and implemented while design workflow work ran.
Parallel did not defer all implementation until investigations completed; it built and tested the solution while workflow investigations were still running.
The indispensable implementation and local verification path received enough parent attention to produce a 38/38 passing artifact; the direct issue is verifier failure takeover.
Although workflows consumed budget, the retained episode is one aborted verifier workflow with no takeover, not proven collective fan-out exhaustion displacing implementation.
The verifier brief was broad, but the observed adverse event is killed workflow plus no takeover; scope alone does not establish an oversized-child pattern.
The verifier workflow state shows a detailed brief listing /output files, requirements, read-only rules, and reference binary access; no known requirement omission caused unusable work.
Parallel did not delegate separately owned components requiring an omitted interface contract; children audited or designed while the parent owned submitted code integration.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer; the verifier aggregate never existed because the workflow was killed.
There was no completed large handoff that the parent failed to reduce; the key verifier result remained null.
No receiver acted on superseded workflow information to perform invalid verification or integration.
No incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parallel parent did not present a final whole-task completion decision; it timed out with an empty final response, while official evaluation later passed.
Workflow retry logs show stalled retry attempts, but no replacement child is shown repeating prior work due to absence of inherited checkpoint state.
